pr_title: fix(security-middleware): fix config merging with defaults
pr_body:
<!--

To help us merge your PR, make sure to follow the instructions below:

Please ensure you read the Contributing Guide: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

### What does it do?

Fixes merging logic in security middleware configuration.

### Why is it needed?

Currently, security middleware ignores user custom CSP rules for the directives `script-src/connect-src`, which blocks loading any custom scripts.

### How to test it?

1. Set custom script-src CSP rules in security middleware configuration `config/middleware`. Example:

```js
// config/middleware.ts
export default [
  'strapi::logger',
  'strapi::errors',
  {
    name: 'strapi::security',
    config: {
      contentSecurityPolicy: {
        useDefaults: true,
        directives: {
          'connect-src': ["'self'", 'https:'],
          'script-src': ["'self'", 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net', 'https://unpkg.com'],
          upgradeInsecureRequests: null,
        },
      },
    },
  },
  ...
];
```

2. Start and request admin page from strapi server, and verify that custom CSP rules are respected.

```sh
curl -v https://localhost:1337/admin 2>&1 | grep content-security-policy
```

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

This fixes #19589.

issue_context.title: Custom CSP rules in security middleware are ignored
issue_context.body:
<!--

Before you start, please make sure your issue is understandable and reproducible.

Please ensure you have also read and understand the contributing guide.

https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-an-issue
-->

## Bug report

### Required System information

<!-- Please ensure you are using the Node LTS version (v18 or v20) -->
<!-- Strapi v3 is no longer supported, please update to Strapi v4 -->
<!-- If you are reporting a frontend bug please provide error logs after setting STRAPI_ENFORCE_SOURCEMAPS=true in your .env -->
<!-- This environment variable makes frontend errors easier to read and trace -->

- Node.js version: v20
- Yarn version: 3.1.1
- Strapi version: v4.20.1
- Database: Postgres
- Operating system: Linux 
- Is your project Javascript or Typescript: Typescript

<!-- Did you know you can run `yarn strapi report` or `npm run strapi report` to get this information easier? -->

### Describe the bug

Custom Content Security Policy directives configured in security middleware are ignored for '/admin' path. 

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Go to `config/middleware.ts`, and add custom `script-src` rule for CSP, example:
```js
// config/middleware.ts
export default [
  'strapi::logger',
  'strapi::errors',
  {
    name: 'strapi::security',
    config: {
      contentSecurityPolicy: {
        useDefaults: true,
        directives: {
          'connect-src': ["'self'", 'https:'],
          'script-src': ["'self'", 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net', 'https://unpkg.com'],
          upgradeInsecureRequests: null,
        },
      },
    },
  },
  ...
];
```
3. Request the `/admin` from Strapi server, and verify the CSP header includes the custom rules configured above :x:
```sh
curl -v https://localhost:1337/admin 2>&1 | grep content-security-policy
```

### Expected behavior

The CSP header should include the custom rules I configured in security middleware.

### Additional context

This bug was introduced here https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/18697/files#r1440289055.  `lodash/merge` was used to merge CSP policies, and it has an unexpected behavior with arrays https://github.com/lodash/lodash/issues/5384. The fix replaces `merge` with `mergeWith` with custom handler for array values.

On the side, `unsafe-inline` is unsafe and should preferably be enabled only in DEV mode. This hack seems related to the work on vite (having vite would be great :rocket:).

review_comments:
This kind of merging prevents overwritting completly and should be avoided. 

You can inverse the merge order so that user config will override the default one when provided below
